text:
alex: Quick heads-up: I made a tiny sample that demonstrates three different bundlers picking different entrypoints for the JS SDK and each failing differently when deployed to an edge runtime (Cloudflare/Netlify Edge). Posting steps + logs so we can add a short devex doc.

lee: please paste repro and how to run.

alex: repo is minimal: package.json has \"exports\" map with import/require and a \"browser\" override. code is just an import + client init. Commands: npm ci && npm run build:{vite|rollup|webpack} then run the generated bundle in the edge shim (I used @miniflare for CF).

package.json (relevant):
```
{
  "name": "repro-edge-resolve",
  "type": "module",
  "exports": {
    ".": {
      "browser": "./dist/browser.cjs.js",
      "import": "./dist/index.esm.js",
      "require": "./dist/index.cjs.js"
    },
    "./*": "./dist/*"
  }
}
```

src/main.ts:
```ts
import { createClient } from 'redwood-inference';
const c = createClient({ apiKey: process.env.RI_KEY });
console.log('ok', typeof c);
```

Vite build -> miniflare run -> runtime: Uncaught ReferenceError: process is not defined
Rollup build (with @rollup/plugin-commonjs) -> build succeeds but runtime: TypeError: createClient is not a function (default interop issue)
Webpack build -> bundle contains small helper that uses globalThis.process or __dirname and fails in edge: ReferenceError: __dirname is not defined

maria: interesting. Sounds like 3 separate failure classes: missing node globals, cjs/esm default interop, and bundler choosing the "browser" condition which points to a cjs build with node-specific helpers removed but still using process in a helper.

sam: note: esbuild-based bundlers (vite's build uses esbuild for deps) follow export conditions differently from rollup/webpack. Also the presence of a "browser" condition can move resolution toward a file that assumed browser polyfills and accidentally left a leftover `process` usage.

lee: what quick fixes did you try?

alex: matrix of local fixes: 
- Vite: set build.target to 'es2022', and alias 'redwood-inference' -> 'node_modules/redwood-inference/dist/index.esm.js' plus set define: { 'process.env': '{}' } for the build. That removes process at runtime in my miniflare run.
- Rollup: configure @rollup/plugin-commonjs with `requireReturnsDefault: 'namespace'` and add `resolve({ exportConditions: ['import', 'node', 'default'] })`. That fixed the createClient import.
- Webpack: set `resolve.conditionNames = ['import', 'default']` and add `plugins: [ new webpack.DefinePlugin({ 'process.env.NODE_ENV': JSON.stringify('production') }) ]` and `resolve.fallback = { fs: false, path: false }`. This produced a smaller bundle that runs in edge.

maria: those are good local workarounds. Longer-term SDK changes we should consider in the issue: publish a dedicated `exports` condition for \"edge\" (e.g., "edge": "./dist/index.edge.mjs") that is pure ESM, uses no node helpers, and guarantees typings at package root. Bundlers could then prefer the edge condition when consumers set conditionNames accordingly.

sam: also consider adding a tiny package.json field: "sideEffects": false and a separate `types` root entry so TS consumers don't need to point at the .js file. Many TS users get caught when they alias the .js ESM file and lose declared types.

ci-bot: CI job failed: ci/bundler-smoke (PR #1401) - see https://ci.internal/jobs/1401 - webpack smoke failed on netlify-edge shim.

lee: for the devex doc we should list per-bundler repro + minimal fix: 
- Vite: alias to ESM, define process env, remove ssr.noExternal for build or add ssr: { target: 'web' } depending on app.
- Rollup: ensure resolve plugin exportConditions includes 'import', use commonjs plugin `requireReturnsDefault: 'auto'` and `esModule: true` where needed.
- Webpack: prefer import condition via `resolve.conditionNames`, ProvidePlugin/DefinePlugin for process.env, and fallbacks for node builtins.

maria: additional note: point consumers to `node_modules/redwood-inference/package.json` -> if they see a browser condition, their bundler might resolve that path first. For CI we should add a smoke test that builds a tiny sample with each bundler in a matrix and runs it in our edge shim (miniflare). That will catch regressions from future SDK builds.

alex: filed issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/305 with the sample repo and logs. I'll draft the devex doc and a small CI job template.

sam: thanks. One more trick: if you can't change package exports immediately, provide a tiny compatibility entry `redwood-inference/edge` that re-exports the ESM client and has its own package entry (so consumers can `import from 'redwood-inference/edge'`). That avoids consumers needing to mess with bundler configs.

alex: good suggestion. I'll add that to the PR. If anyone wants to reproduce fast: clone repo, npm i, npm run build:vite && node ./dist/vite/entry.js (or use miniflare). Repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repro-edge-resolve (branch: alex/edge-resolve).
